claim: The interlink-slurm-plugin ships a Tsocks configuration option, described as enabling 'proxy networking' and 'only implemented for the Slurm sidecar at the moment,' whose TsocksLoginNode setting is documented as providing an SSH-based 'window to the external world' for the Slurm job.
stance_target: a Slurm-backed virtual pod gets a normal, directly cluster-routable pod IP that an inference router could dial into
quoted_support: Tsocks | true or false values only. Enables or Disables the use of tsocks library to allow proxy networking. Only implemented for the Slurm sidecar at the moment. | TsocksLoginNode | specify an existing node to ssh to. It will be your "window to the external world"

claim: The Slurm sidecar plugin executes pod containers as Slurm batch jobs via Singularity/Apptainer, with pod ConfigMaps and Secrets exported and mounted as files into the Singularity container rather than injected through native Kubernetes secret/volume mechanisms.
stance_target: how faithfully a Slurm-backed virtual pod reproduces normal Kubernetes pod semantics
quoted_support: ExportPodData | Set it to true if you want to export Pod's ConfigMaps and Secrets as mountpoints in your Singularity Container
